problem.h2: Four problems. One missing data layer.
problem.rhs: Compliance, cost, politics, science — four pressures on the sector, all blocked by the same data gap.
problem.meta1_v: EU traceability mandate from January 2026 — data required, not yet captured at sector scale.
problem.meta2_v: Margins erode trip by trip with no per-haul fuel evidence on board.
problem.meta3_v: Quota debates run without operational evidence from the fleet.
problem.meta4_v: Stock models rely on infrequent surveys, not continuous fleet data.
problem.closer: NaviTools was built to capture this missing data layer.
fisherman.h2: The technology that takes work off the deck.
fisherman.rhs: NaviTools was conceived by a former skipper. Every feature is measured against one question: does it save time, money, or trouble on board?
fisherman.h3: Less paperwork. Sharper margin. Evidence on file.
fisherman.li1_term: Your e-logbook data, prepared for you.
fisherman.li1_text: Position, depth, gear, species, weights and discards are captured from sensors all trip long. When it is time to submit the e-logbook, the fields are ready — you confirm, you do not type.
fisherman.li2_term: Full EU traceability, hold to buyer.
fisherman.li2_text: NaviTools delivers the complete traceability solution the EU now requires. Each box is fixed to a position in the hold (FishGrid), scanned once by RFID at landing, and tracked through the auction to the buyer — end-to-end, on every trip. Already implemented on five vessels (below).
fisherman.li3_term: Fuel cost per haul, per trip, per kilo of fish.
fisherman.li3_text: Liters per hour live. Liters per kilo of catch the moment a haul comes on deck. Spot the tow that earned nothing. See in euros whether a hull cleaning, a new propeller or a different RPM actually paid back.
fisherman.li4_term: Evidence on file before it's asked for.
fisherman.li4_text: Net damage, gear loss, auction-weight disputes, near-misses: position, depth, course, hydraulic pressure and per-box catch composition are timestamped and stored. Insurance, surveyor, lawyer — the record is there when they need it.
fisherman.li5_term: Your grounds, mapped from your own hauls.
fisherman.li5_text: Catch-per-hour by depth, bottom type and season — built trip after trip from data you already generate. The pattern no skipper can hold in their head over a 20-year career, written down and searchable.
fisherman.li6_term: Margin per trip, while you are still fishing.
fisherman.li6_text: Catch value minus fuel burn minus crew share, recalculated as each haul lands. Visserij Verduurzaamt premium tracked separately. Stay or steam — decide with numbers, not just gut feel.
fisherman.reg_body: From January 2026, the EU traceability obligation requires every commercial fishing vessel to record and transmit catch data with a new level of granularity. NaviTools fleets are already there.
fisherman.precedent_lead: Full traceability is not a plan. It is already implemented on five vessels.

tech.h2: Built on deliberate choices — not on hype.
tech.rhs: NaviTools is a system, not a single product: vessel-hardened hardware, enterprise cloud, open-source scientific modules, and a new generation of AI tools that turn raw signal into decisions.
tech.c1_caption: Minister of Agriculture & Fisheries Hilde Crevits holding the BleuBox, with Pedro Rappé.
tech.c1_desc: Purpose-built collection unit, hardened for working vessels. Dedicated processing, minimal maintenance, long service life.
tech.c2_desc: Data processing and storage on enterprise-grade cloud infrastructure — the same standards used by global research institutions and governments. Reliable, scalable, auditable.
tech.c3_desc: Research modules — stock assessment, species distribution, environmental data pipelines — plug in as modular, open-source components. No black boxes.
tech.c4_caption: "W-145's skipper Geert van der Plas is positive about the benefits of gathering data."
tech.c4_desc: Conceived from the deck up, by a former commercial skipper. Practical first, data-rich second, complex only when necessary.
tech.c5_desc: Vessel owners retain full ownership of their data. They decide who accesses it, on what terms, for which purpose.
tech.c6_desc: AI agents handle the heavy work: crunching trip data, building dashboards, running predictive models that sharpen as more vessels contribute. On deck, the same agents make that data accessible in plain language — a skipper or fleet manager can ask a question and get an answer on their own phone or tablet. No new interface to learn — the data comes to them.
